summary: The study investigates the self-limiting mechanism of chloride atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) on GaAs surfaces using in situ optical characterization. The process involves alternating supply of GaCl and AsH3 at specific temperatures, and the self-limiting behavior is observed through changes in reflection intensity and anisotropic surface bonds.
evidence: The reflection intensity varied by several percent depending on the source gas supply sequence. The saturation of the reflection intensity change during the GaCl supply is considered to be due to the self-limiting mechanism in chloride ALE. A similar saturation of reflection intensity was also observed from 400 to 600 “C. This result corresponds to the existence of the self-limiting mechanism over a wide temperature range.
